pages.lesson:
LESSON: INTEGERS SIMPLE AND COMBINED OPERATIONS ON INTEGERS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.1: Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we carry out operations of integers in real-life situations?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. perform basic operations on Integers in different situations
2. apply Integers to real- life situations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss with peers and work out basic operations on integers using number cards and charts,
2. Play games involving numbers and operations by picking integers and performing all basic operations,
3. Critical thinking and Problem-solving: interpretation and inference: as learners work out combined operations of integers in the correct order.
4. Learning to Learn: organising own learning as learners carry out activities such as reading temperature changes in a thermometer and discussing how to record it.
5. Digital Literacy: interacting with technologies; as learners use IT devices to determine temperature. Values

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we carry out operations of integers in real-life situations?
2. How do we apply integers in daily activities?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
